edition.alertText: Oil rebounds 4% on fresh tanker attacks as Iran reports 5 vessels hit mines — Brent settles at $98.29, WTI at $90.52; Trump weighs strikes or deal in lame-duck window — authority runs until Jan 3 when new Congress convenes; Vance privately criticizes Netanyahu and urges agreement; Qatar mediators propose 3-day confidence-building sequence; Araghchi offers 2-day plan: US measures day 1, Hormuz reopens day 2; Eurasia Group cuts Iran deal odds from 20% to 10%; Iran FM Araghchi calls 6 regional foreign ministers including Saudi Prince Faisal; UKMTO reports tanker struck by 2 projectiles 50nm north of Qatar; IRGC claims 2 supertankers and tugboat caught fire from mines on 'unauthorized' route; October saw record 35 ship attacks — highest monthly total of the war; gold surges to $4,088 on lame-duck uncertainty and dollar weakness; Brent heading for 15%+ weekly loss, WTI ~12%; Saudi warns of danger near Yanbu Red Sea hub as Houthi attacks continue; South Korea to deploy maritime patrol aircraft near Hormuz; US Treasury sanctions Indian nationals aiding Iran's shadow fleet; Houthis demand $51B from Saudi Arabia to end war (WSJ); Democrats vow to use funding powers to end conflict; Hegseth's job reportedly in question; GACA extends King Khalid airport suspension; US gas ~$4.10/gal

situation: The Strait of Hormuz crisis reached day 252 as the post-midterm political landscape reshaped both the diplomatic track and the threat of renewed escalation. With Democrats set to control both chambers of Congress from January 2027, the focus shifted to the 58-day lame-duck window during which Trump retains full war authority. Trump told the Financial Times he had no immediate plans to order new strikes but warned of a possible 'heavy hit,' while CIA Director Ratcliffe and Treasury Secretary Bessent reportedly favor maintaining the naval blockade over military escalation. Vice President Vance, who blamed the Iran war for the Republican midterm rout, privately criticized Netanyahu and urged an agreement — reportedly reaching out to Iranian official Rezaei about ceasefire terms. Qatar intensified mediation, with mediators proposing a three-day confidence-building sequence and seeking backing from both sides. Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi called six regional counterparts including Saudi Arabia's Prince Faisal bin Farhan, and reiterated his two-day plan: the US takes measures on day one and Hormuz reopens on day two. But Eurasia Group cut its probability of a deal from 20% to 10% and raised the odds of a prolonged standoff to 30%, warning that Brent could spike to $110–125 if escalation resumes. Democrats in Congress signaled immediate action, with Schumer vowing 'this war must end' and Rep. Ro Khanna proposing a continuing resolution barring funding for combat in Iran. Defense Secretary Hegseth faces calls for accountability, with his job reportedly in question.

Oil markets whipsawed as Brent crude settled at $98.29 on November 5, up $3.67 (+3.88%), recovering from the midterm sell-off after fresh tanker attacks revived supply fears. WTI climbed to $90.52 (+2.72%). Despite the rebound, Brent was heading for a weekly loss exceeding 15% — the steepest since the war began — while WTI was down approximately 12% on the week. Gold surged to $4,088/oz (+4.50%) as uncertainty over Trump's lame-duck intentions and Bank of England rate hikes drove safe-haven demand, rebounding sharply from Wednesday's post-midterm low of $3,912. Newcastle coal eased to $145.20/tonne (-0.68%) as the broader energy complex adjusted to shifting ceasefire expectations. VLCC fixtures for Arabian Gulf routes partially recovered from their midterm plunge, with AG-China rates estimated in the $400K–440K/day range, up from the $380K–420K lows on November 4 but still well below the $469K level from November 3. Saudi crude exports averaged 5.52 million bpd in October (Kpler), down from roughly 7 million bpd pre-war. The Breakwave bi-weekly report confirmed October Hormuz crude flows at approximately 11.7 million b/d, up from 9.8 million in September but still 19% below the pre-war baseline. About 80 VLCCs remain in Gulf-of-Oman shuttle operations with 23-day average round voyages versus 9–10 optimal. US gasoline fell to approximately $4.10/gal (AAA) as the oil price crash began filtering through to pump prices.

The maritime situation intensified even as diplomatic channels remained open. Iranian forces reported at least five tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz on November 5 — the IRGC said two tankers and a tugboat hit mines on 'unauthorized' routes, while the Iranian army reported three more vessels struck mines in an 'unsafe area' east of the strait. Separately, UKMTO reported a tanker struck by two projectiles approximately 50 nautical miles north of Madinat ash Shamal, Qatar. October recorded 35 ship attacks — the highest monthly total of the war — and the pace in early November is approaching that record, with JMIC reporting four attacks in 52 hours off Oman's Musandam coast between November 1 and 3. The estimated wartime attack total now stands at approximately 212 incidents. UKMTO acknowledged it is 'struggling to accurately report' the true number of attacks because most ships refuse to report them. CENTCOM has redirected 144 vessels since the blockade resumed, with about 31 US-assisted transits per day — slightly below the 34/day October average. Saudi Arabia warned of danger near Yanbu, its Red Sea export hub, as Houthi attacks continued — GACA extended the King Khalid International Airport suspension after a Houthi missile claim, and the Houthis are reportedly demanding $51 billion from Saudi Arabia to end the war (WSJ). South Korea announced deployment of maritime patrol aircraft and an explosive ordnance disposal team near Hormuz. The US Treasury sanctioned a network of Indian nationals accused of operating fraudulent ship registries for Iran's shadow fleet. QatarEnergy's LNG force majeure remains in effect through December 2026, and fertilizer shipments through Hormuz remain at zero for the fourth consecutive month.

supplyChain.name: Sulfur
supplyChain.text: Global exports down 39% YoY to 6.1M tonnes in Q2 (S&P). Sulfur prices above $1,000/tonne — more than doubled since pre-war — feeding into phosphate production costs; Egypt, Brazil, India cutting output. Mosaic phosphate plants remain curtailed including South Fort Meade (Florida) — 199 workers laid off. Morocco's OCP needs 3.7M tonnes/yr from the region. Nearly half of seaborne sulfur passed through Hormuz pre-war. Phosphate prices up 25-30%. Trade routes shifting as Morocco and China seek alternative sources (ChemAnalyst).

supplyChain.name: Sulfuric Acid
supplyChain.text: China banned exports Apr-Aug (700kt/yr quota replaced). SX-EW copper producers (15% of global cathode) fully exposed. Huayou cut Indonesian nickel HPAL output 50%.

supplyChain.name: Fertilizer
supplyChain.text: Fertilizer shipments through Hormuz at zero for fourth consecutive month — September, October, and early November all zero (World Visualized/Syz Group/Fertilizer Daily). Urea exports from Hormuz-dependent economies fell 83% YoY in April (ITC). ~850kt urea stranded. 4 of 5 Bangladesh urea plants shut since March due to LNG shortages. Pakistan faces 200,000-ton fertiliser shortfall (Express Tribune). FAO Food Price Index at 136 (highest since Nov 2022). World Bank: fertilizer prices surging as Hormuz disruptions tighten supplies. India building two fertiliser futures — diversifying sources while lobbying for corridor (Diplomat Magazine). Urea-to-corn ratio at 126 bushels/tonne vs 75 in Dec 2025 (CSIS). IFPRI: no bypass route for ammonia or sulfur unlike crude. UN fertilizer corridor stalled pending US-Iran agreement. Hormuz crude recovery hides slower one for LNG, fertilizer, helium and aluminum — non-oil flows still near zero (Enterprise AM). Out of Hormuz energy shocks, the ingredients for a global food crisis intensify (PRNewswire/IFA).

supplyChain.name: LNG
supplyChain.text: QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure through end of December 2026 — 8th consecutive extension since April. Global LNG supply gap estimated at ~600 bcf. Dutch TTF gas at €97.53/MWh (~$108.51), highest since 2022 energy crisis. Pakistan to pay >$1B for winter LNG spot cargoes at ~2x Qatari contract price. Qatari LNG carrier Al Mayeda struck near Hormuz (Oct 31). Bangladesh struggling with spot market costs. Lufthansa says 2026 fuel costs €2B higher amid Iran war. Europe and Asia face tight supply heading into winter. JERA CEO says Qatar LNG supply unlikely to recover soon.

supplyChain.name: Petrochemicals
supplyChain.text: MEG ethylene/polyethylene exports disrupted. Gulf petrochem complex cut to ~60% capacity. Methanol down 80% (ITC). Dow, LyondellBasell margins widening on supply constraint. ExxonMobil Q3 profit more than doubled to $15.4B on energy surge. Aramco Q3 profit surges 34.6% to $36.3B.
